lessons.title: Desired state
lessons.summary: Terraform configuration declares infrastructure objects and their desired attributes.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Terraform configuration declares infrastructure objects and their desired attributes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Providers read remote objects and Terraform compares configuration, state and reality to plan actions. Configuration describes a goal, not a guaranteed sequence of shell commands. Review the proposed changes before allowing writes.

lessons.takeaway: Providers read remote objects and Terraform compares configuration, state and reality to plan actions. Configuration describes a goal, not a guaranteed sequence of shell commands. Review the proposed changes before allowing writes.

lessons.title: Initialization
lessons.summary: Initialization prepares a working directory with backend configuration, provider plugins and referenced modules.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Initialization prepares a working directory with backend configuration, provider plugins and referenced modules.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Run init after cloning or changing dependencies and backend settings. Backend migration and reconfiguration have different effects, so inspect prompts carefully. Initialization alone does not provision the declared resources.

lessons.takeaway: Run init after cloning or changing dependencies and backend settings. Backend migration and reconfiguration have different effects, so inspect prompts carefully. Initialization alone does not provision the declared resources.

lessons.title: Planning
lessons.summary: A plan previews actions needed to reconcile managed infrastructure with configuration.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A plan previews actions needed to reconcile managed infrastructure with configuration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Normal planning refreshes remote values, computes a dependency graph and shows creates, updates, replacements and deletes. A speculative plan can become stale. Save and review the plan used for a controlled apply.

lessons.takeaway: Normal planning refreshes remote values, computes a dependency graph and shows creates, updates, replacements and deletes. A speculative plan can become stale. Save and review the plan used for a controlled apply.

lessons.title: State mapping
lessons.summary: Terraform state maps configuration resource addresses to remote object identities and tracked attributes.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Terraform state maps configuration resource addresses to remote object identities and tracked attributes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Without the mapping, Terraform cannot reliably distinguish existing managed objects from objects it should create. State may contain secrets. Protect access, versioning and locking, and use supported state operations instead of hand-editing JSON.

lessons.takeaway: Without the mapping, Terraform cannot reliably distinguish existing managed objects from objects it should create. State may contain secrets. Protect access, versioning and locking, and use supported state operations instead of hand-editing JSON.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.summary: Input variables parameterize a module's configuration.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Input variables parameterize a module's configuration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Types and validation constrain accepted values; callers provide inputs through documented mechanisms with defined precedence. Defaults should be safe for the intended environment. A sensitive flag hides some display output but does not encrypt stored values.

lessons.takeaway: Types and validation constrain accepted values; callers provide inputs through documented mechanisms with defined precedence. Defaults should be safe for the intended environment. A sensitive flag hides some display output but does not encrypt stored values.

lessons.title: Outputs
lessons.summary: Outputs expose selected values from a module to callers or users.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Outputs expose selected values from a module to callers or users.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Child-module outputs are referenced by the parent; root outputs can be displayed through the CLI. Sensitive outputs need access controls because machine-readable or raw output may reveal them. Avoid exporting entire resource objects unnecessarily.

lessons.takeaway: Child-module outputs are referenced by the parent; root outputs can be displayed through the CLI. Sensitive outputs need access controls because machine-readable or raw output may reveal them. Avoid exporting entire resource objects unnecessarily.

lessons.title: Providers
lessons.summary: Providers implement the API-specific operations Terraform uses to manage resources and data sources.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Providers implement the API-specific operations Terraform uses to manage resources and data sources.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Configuration selects provider settings and aliases; version constraints and lock files control plugin selection. Changing a provider version can alter schemas and behavior. Test upgrades and inspect resulting plans before applying.

lessons.takeaway: Configuration selects provider settings and aliases; version constraints and lock files control plugin selection. Changing a provider version can alter schemas and behavior. Test upgrades and inspect resulting plans before applying.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.summary: A module groups related Terraform configuration behind inputs and outputs.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A module groups related Terraform configuration behind inputs and outputs.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Reusable modules encapsulate a stable interface while root modules define deployable boundaries. Pin external module sources appropriately and avoid hiding every setting behind an oversized abstraction. A module does not automatically create a separate state or permission boundary.

lessons.takeaway: Reusable modules encapsulate a stable interface while root modules define deployable boundaries. Pin external module sources appropriately and avoid hiding every setting behind an oversized abstraction. A module does not automatically create a separate state or permission boundary.

lessons.title: Lock files
lessons.summary: The dependency lock file records selected provider versions and package checksums.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The dependency lock file records selected provider versions and package checksums.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Commit it so collaborators and CI use consistent provider selections. Version constraints still define allowed upgrades; init -upgrade intentionally reselects within those constraints. The provider lock file does not pin remote module versions.

lessons.takeaway: Commit it so collaborators and CI use consistent provider selections. Version constraints still define allowed upgrades; init -upgrade intentionally reselects within those constraints. The provider lock file does not pin remote module versions.

lessons.title: Remote state
lessons.summary: A remote backend stores state outside the local working directory.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A remote backend stores state outside the local working directory.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Central storage supports team access, durability and, depending on backend, locking. Enforce encryption, version recovery and least privilege. Remote state consumers may need access to more state data than the output interface suggests.

lessons.takeaway: Central storage supports team access, durability and, depending on backend, locking. Enforce encryption, version recovery and least privilege. Remote state consumers may need access to more state data than the output interface suggests.

lessons.title: State locking
lessons.summary: State locking prevents cooperating Terraform operations from writing the same state concurrently.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: State locking prevents cooperating Terraform operations from writing the same state concurrently.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Lock support and configuration depend on the backend. A lock error may represent an active operation, so identify its owner before intervention. Force-unlocking a live writer risks divergent state and conflicting remote operations.

lessons.takeaway: Lock support and configuration depend on the backend. A lock error may represent an active operation, so identify its owner before intervention. Force-unlocking a live writer risks divergent state and conflicting remote operations.

lessons.title: Sensitive values
lessons.summary: Sensitive values are marked to reduce accidental exposure in human-facing output.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Sensitive values are marked to reduce accidental exposure in human-facing output.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Marking a value sensitive does not remove it from state or saved plans. Control artifact storage, logs and backend permissions. Review provider behavior and avoid using secrets in names, tags or other inherently visible fields.

lessons.takeaway: Marking a value sensitive does not remove it from state or saved plans. Control artifact storage, logs and backend permissions. Review provider behavior and avoid using secrets in names, tags or other inherently visible fields.

lessons.title: Resource addresses
lessons.summary: A resource address identifies a resource or instance in Terraform configuration and state.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A resource address identifies a resource or instance in Terraform configuration and state.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Addresses include module paths and instance keys for count or for_each. Refactoring an address without a migration declaration can appear as destroy-and-create. Quote addresses containing brackets or keys correctly in shell commands.

lessons.takeaway: Addresses include module paths and instance keys for count or for_each. Refactoring an address without a migration declaration can appear as destroy-and-create. Quote addresses containing brackets or keys correctly in shell commands.

lessons.title: Count indexing
lessons.summary: count creates instances identified by numeric positions.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: count creates instances identified by numeric positions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Removing an element from the middle of an input list can shift identities and trigger unintended replacements. for_each with stable keys is often more appropriate for named infrastructure. Changing the instance scheme needs an explicit state migration.

lessons.takeaway: Removing an element from the middle of an input list can shift identities and trigger unintended replacements. for_each with stable keys is often more appropriate for named infrastructure. Changing the instance scheme needs an explicit state migration.

lessons.title: Dependencies
lessons.summary: Terraform dependencies determine ordering constraints in its operation graph.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Terraform dependencies determine ordering constraints in its operation graph.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: References create implicit dependencies; depends_on adds an explicit relationship when data flow does not express it. Unnecessary broad dependencies can increase unknown values and serialization. Dependency order does not by itself mean an application is ready to serve.

lessons.takeaway: References create implicit dependencies; depends_on adds an explicit relationship when data flow does not express it. Unnecessary broad dependencies can increase unknown values and serialization. Dependency order does not by itself mean an application is ready to serve.

lessons.title: Data sources
lessons.summary: Data sources read existing external information for use in configuration.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Data sources read existing external information for use in configuration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They do not usually take lifecycle ownership of the queried object. Values may be unknown until apply if they depend on planned changes. Make selection criteria stable so a broad lookup does not silently select a different image or network.

lessons.takeaway: They do not usually take lifecycle ownership of the queried object. Values may be unknown until apply if they depend on planned changes. Make selection criteria stable so a broad lookup does not silently select a different image or network.

lessons.title: Import
lessons.summary: Import associates an existing remote object with a Terraform resource address.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Import associates an existing remote object with a Terraform resource address.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The configuration must also describe the desired object. Import alone does not guarantee the next plan is empty or safe; defaults and mismatched attributes can trigger changes. Review ownership and the post-import plan before applying.

lessons.takeaway: The configuration must also describe the desired object. Import alone does not guarantee the next plan is empty or safe; defaults and mismatched attributes can trigger changes. Review ownership and the post-import plan before applying.

lessons.title: Moved blocks
lessons.summary: Moved blocks describe address changes during a configuration refactor.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Moved blocks describe address changes during a configuration refactor.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Terraform uses them to preserve the mapping to an existing object instead of treating the old and new addresses as unrelated resources. Test migrations from supported previous versions and retain migration history when downstream users may upgrade later.

lessons.takeaway: Terraform uses them to preserve the mapping to an existing object instead of treating the old and new addresses as unrelated resources. Test migrations from supported previous versions and retain migration history when downstream users may upgrade later.

lessons.title: Lifecycle protection
lessons.summary: Lifecycle rules adjust planning behavior for managed resources.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Lifecycle rules adjust planning behavior for managed resources.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: prevent_destroy rejects plans that destroy a protected configured resource, but it is not a backup or universal deletion guard. Removing the resource block removes that configuration-based protection. Pair lifecycle settings with permissions and recovery procedures.

lessons.takeaway: prevent_destroy rejects plans that destroy a protected configured resource, but it is not a backup or universal deletion guard. Removing the resource block removes that configuration-based protection. Pair lifecycle settings with permissions and recovery procedures.

lessons.title: Ignored changes
lessons.summary: ignore_changes excludes selected attribute differences from normal update planning.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: ignore_changes excludes selected attribute differences from normal update planning.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It can support shared ownership with an external controller, but also hides drift. Specify the narrowest attributes and document who owns them. Ignoring everything can leave Terraform showing stability while important security or capacity settings diverge.

lessons.takeaway: It can support shared ownership with an external controller, but also hides drift. Specify the narrowest attributes and document who owns them. Ignoring everything can leave Terraform showing stability while important security or capacity settings diverge.

lessons.title: Replacement order
lessons.summary: A replacement creates a new object and removes the old one because some attributes cannot change in place.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A replacement creates a new object and removes the old one because some attributes cannot change in place.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: create_before_destroy can reduce downtime when names, quotas and dependencies allow overlap. It cannot make an incompatible database migration safe or bypass uniqueness constraints. Review the graph and temporary capacity requirements.

lessons.takeaway: create_before_destroy can reduce downtime when names, quotas and dependencies allow overlap. It cannot make an incompatible database migration safe or bypass uniqueness constraints. Review the graph and temporary capacity requirements.

lessons.title: Targeted applies
lessons.summary: Targeted operations restrict Terraform's attention to selected resources and necessary dependencies.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Targeted operations restrict Terraform's attention to selected resources and necessary dependencies.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They are useful for exceptional recovery but can leave the wider configuration unreconciled. Run a full plan afterward and resolve remaining drift. Routine targeted applies undermine confidence that the declared system matches reality.

lessons.takeaway: They are useful for exceptional recovery but can leave the wider configuration unreconciled. Run a full plan afterward and resolve remaining drift. Routine targeted applies undermine confidence that the declared system matches reality.

lessons.title: Provisioners
lessons.summary: Provisioners run scripts or copy files as part of selected resource lifecycle events.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Provisioners run scripts or copy files as part of selected resource lifecycle events.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Terraform has limited understanding of what a script changed and how to undo it. Prefer images, cloud-init or configuration-management tools when possible. Script failure may leave partially configured resources requiring explicit recovery.

lessons.takeaway: Terraform has limited understanding of what a script changed and how to undo it. Prefer images, cloud-init or configuration-management tools when possible. Script failure may leave partially configured resources requiring explicit recovery.

lessons.title: Workspace boundaries
lessons.summary: CLI workspaces maintain separate state instances for one working configuration.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: CLI workspaces maintain separate state instances for one working configuration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They can separate similar deployments, but do not automatically isolate credentials, permissions or backend administration. Strong production boundaries may require separate roots, backends and identities. Always verify the selected workspace before planning.

lessons.takeaway: They can separate similar deployments, but do not automatically isolate credentials, permissions or backend administration. Strong production boundaries may require separate roots, backends and identities. Always verify the selected workspace before planning.

lessons.title: Saved plans
lessons.summary: A saved plan captures the intended actions and relevant values for a later apply.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A saved plan captures the intended actions and relevant values for a later apply.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Applying the file executes that planned decision rather than asking for a fresh interactive approval. Protect it as potentially sensitive and bind it to the reviewed commit and target. Discard stale plans after relevant changes.

lessons.takeaway: Applying the file executes that planned decision rather than asking for a fresh interactive approval. Protect it as potentially sensitive and bind it to the reviewed commit and target. Discard stale plans after relevant changes.

lessons.title: Drift policy
lessons.summary: Drift is a difference between declared or recorded configuration and remote reality.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Drift is a difference between declared or recorded configuration and remote reality.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A team policy decides whether to revert an out-of-band change or adopt it into code. Refresh-only planning updates the proposed state view without requesting configuration reconciliation. Inspect evidence before overriding an emergency mitigation.

lessons.takeaway: A team policy decides whether to revert an out-of-band change or adopt it into code. Refresh-only planning updates the proposed state view without requesting configuration reconciliation. Inspect evidence before overriding an emergency mitigation.

lessons.title: State splitting
lessons.summary: State splitting moves ownership into smaller independently managed deployment boundaries.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: State splitting moves ownership into smaller independently managed deployment boundaries.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Choose boundaries around lifecycle, team ownership and blast radius rather than arbitrary file size. Plan object-address migrations and dependency interfaces, and ensure no resource is simultaneously managed by two states. Maintain recovery copies during migration.

lessons.takeaway: Choose boundaries around lifecycle, team ownership and blast radius rather than arbitrary file size. Plan object-address migrations and dependency interfaces, and ensure no resource is simultaneously managed by two states. Maintain recovery copies during migration.

lessons.title: Partial failure
lessons.summary: An apply can complete some actions and then fail; it is not a global transaction.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An apply can complete some actions and then fail; it is not a global transaction.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Terraform records successful operations as it proceeds. Inspect state and real resources, fix the cause, and generate a new plan. Retrying blindly or assuming everything rolled back can compound the incident.

lessons.takeaway: Terraform records successful operations as it proceeds. Inspect state and real resources, fix the cause, and generate a new plan. Retrying blindly or assuming everything rolled back can compound the incident.

lessons.title: Provider upgrades
lessons.summary: Provider upgrades change the plugin implementation used to interpret and operate resources.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Provider upgrades change the plugin implementation used to interpret and operate resources.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Review release notes, constraints and lock-file changes; test representative plans in a safe environment. Schema migrations and changed defaults can affect existing state. Do not combine a broad provider upgrade with unrelated high-risk infrastructure changes.

lessons.takeaway: Review release notes, constraints and lock-file changes; test representative plans in a safe environment. Schema migrations and changed defaults can affect existing state. Do not combine a broad provider upgrade with unrelated high-risk infrastructure changes.

lessons.title: Policy checks
lessons.summary: Policy checks evaluate proposed infrastructure against organizational rules.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Policy checks evaluate proposed infrastructure against organizational rules.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Combine syntax validation, plan inspection and checks for requirements such as encryption, tags or approved regions. A passing policy does not prove runtime correctness. Keep exceptions explicit and bind checks to the actual plan being applied.

lessons.takeaway: Combine syntax validation, plan inspection and checks for requirements such as encryption, tags or approved regions. A passing policy does not prove runtime correctness. Keep exceptions explicit and bind checks to the actual plan being applied.

commands.title: Initialize configuration
commands.definition: Initializes the backend, providers and modules for a root configuration.
commands.purpose: Prepare a checked-out configuration before validation or planning.
commands.environment: Can download code and configure or migrate state; use a trusted configuration and review prompts.
commands.interpretation: Read backend prompts and provider selections; initialization success is not infrastructure creation.
commands.safety: Can download code and configure or migrate state; use a trusted configuration and review prompts.

commands.title: Format check
commands.definition: Checks canonical formatting in the directory tree without rewriting files.
commands.purpose: Keep formatting consistent in review and CI.
commands.environment: Does not apply infrastructure changes; run from the intended repository root.
commands.interpretation: Listed filenames need formatting; a nonzero exit signals a formatting issue.
commands.safety: Does not apply infrastructure changes; run from the intended repository root.

commands.title: Validate configuration
commands.definition: Checks configuration syntax and internal consistency after initialization.
commands.purpose: Catch invalid arguments and references before planning.
commands.environment: Read-only validation; provider dependencies must be available.
commands.interpretation: Success confirms structural validity, not credentials, quotas or remote runtime correctness.
commands.safety: Read-only validation; provider dependencies must be available.

commands.title: Review planned changes
commands.definition: Creates a plan and saves it for a later apply.
commands.purpose: Review the actual change set before infrastructure mutation.
commands.environment: Refresh reads remote APIs; saved plans can contain secrets and require protected storage.
commands.expectedOutput: Plan: 1 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
commands.interpretation: + creates, ~ updates, - deletes and -/+ replaces; inspect each replacement and summary.
commands.safety: Refresh reads remote APIs; saved plans can contain secrets and require protected storage.

commands.title: Inspect saved plan
commands.definition: Displays a saved plan in human-readable form.
commands.purpose: Review a plan artifact without applying it.
commands.environment: Read-only; plan content can contain sensitive information.
commands.expectedOutput: # resource address will be updated in-place
commands.interpretation: Check addresses, before/after values and unknown values marked known after apply.
commands.safety: Read-only; plan content can contain sensitive information.

commands.title: Apply reviewed plan
commands.definition: Executes the actions in a saved plan.
commands.purpose: Deploy exactly the reviewed plan instead of generating a new interactive one.
commands.environment: Mutates infrastructure and does not ask for fresh interactive approval for a saved plan; confirm account, workspace and plan provenance first.
commands.interpretation: Inspect per-resource progress and final result; errors may leave partial successful changes.
commands.safety: Mutates infrastructure and does not ask for fresh interactive approval for a saved plan; confirm account, workspace and plan provenance first.

commands.title: List managed addresses
commands.definition: Lists resource addresses recorded in the selected state.
commands.purpose: Locate the exact address before inspection or migration.
commands.environment: Read-only state access; verify backend and workspace.
commands.interpretation: Addresses include module paths and instance keys; presence does not guarantee remote health.
commands.safety: Read-only state access; verify backend and workspace.

commands.title: Inspect managed object
commands.definition: Displays recorded attributes for one managed resource.
commands.purpose: Compare recorded identity with the remote object.
commands.environment: Read-only but may reveal sensitive data; replace and correctly quote the address.
commands.interpretation: The id identifies the remote object; values are recorded state and may need refresh.
commands.safety: Read-only but may reveal sensitive data; replace and correctly quote the address.

commands.title: Show outputs
commands.purpose: Find published endpoints or identifiers after deployment.
commands.environment: Read-only state access; avoid exposing secrets through alternate output modes.
commands.interpretation: Sensitive values are normally redacted in this human-readable view; raw or JSON modes can reveal them.
commands.safety: Read-only state access; avoid exposing secrets through alternate output modes.

commands.title: Current workspace
commands.purpose: Confirm environment selection before planning or applying.
commands.environment: Read-only; also verify credentials and backend configuration.
commands.interpretation: The name identifies a state selection, not an independent permission boundary.
commands.safety: Read-only; also verify credentials and backend configuration.

commands.title: Provider inventory
commands.definition: Shows provider requirements in configuration and state.
commands.purpose: Investigate unexpected plugin dependencies or upgrade scope.
commands.environment: Read-only; actual selected versions are recorded in the lock file.
commands.interpretation: Compare provider source addresses and version constraints across modules.
commands.safety: Read-only; actual selected versions are recorded in the lock file.

commands.title: Drift-only preview
commands.definition: Plans state and output reconciliation with remote changes without proposing normal configuration reconciliation.
commands.purpose: Review out-of-band changes before deciding to adopt or revert them.
commands.environment: Reads remote APIs; do not treat accepting drift as a security or correctness review.
commands.expectedOutput: Objects have changed outside of Terraform
commands.interpretation: Changes describe the refreshed view; applying this plan updates state rather than restoring configuration intent.
commands.safety: Reads remote APIs; do not treat accepting drift as a security or correctness review.

debugging.title: Unexpected replacement after refactor
debugging.symptom: A plan wants to destroy and recreate an unchanged production resource after its module address changed.

steps.evidence: Compare old and new addresses and confirm the remote identity is unchanged. Inspect whether the plan reflects address movement or an actually immutable attribute change.
Add an appropriate moved block or perform a controlled supported state migration. Do not apply a destructive plan merely to align names.
Generate a new full plan and confirm the resource is moved without unwanted replacement and dependent outputs remain correct.

references.title: Unexpected replacement after refactor — primary documentation

debugging.title: State lock conflict
debugging.symptom: A deployment fails because the state is locked.

steps.evidence: Read lock metadata, backend and workspace; identify the owning job and whether it is still active. Check for a concurrent writer before intervening.
Wait for or coordinate with the live operation. Use force-unlock only for a verified stale lock after preserving evidence and confirming no writer remains.
Run a fresh plan with normal locking and verify a single pipeline owns the apply.

debugging.title: Partial apply failure
debugging.symptom: An apply created some resources before failing on a quota or permission error.

steps.evidence: Compare recorded successful resources with remote reality and the error. Do not assume the operation rolled back as a transaction.
Fix the evidenced quota, permission or configuration issue, then create a new full plan. Import or reconcile exceptional unrecorded objects through a controlled process.
Review the new plan for duplicates or deletes, apply safely and verify a subsequent plan has no unexpected changes.

debugging.title: Unplanned console drift
debugging.symptom: A plan would undo a manual production mitigation made during an incident.

steps.evidence: Compare the proposed diff with the incident change record and actual service behavior.
Decide whether to adopt the mitigation into configuration or intentionally revert it after stabilization. Do not blindly apply the old desired state.
Review the resulting plan with the chosen policy and verify the service stays healthy after reconciliation.

debugging.title: Sensitive plan artifact exposed
debugging.symptom: A CI artifact contains credentials despite variables being marked sensitive.

steps.evidence: Determine which values entered saved plans, state or logs and who could access them. Human-output redaction does not remove stored values.
Restrict or remove exposed artifacts under the retention process, rotate compromised credentials and correct artifact access and logging. Keep necessary state recovery controls.
Verify new plans remain protected and new credentials are used successfully without appearing in logs or broadly accessible artifacts.

references.title: Sensitive plan artifact exposed — primary documentation

debugging.title: Count removal replaces wrong instance
debugging.symptom: Removing one middle list item causes multiple resource changes.

steps.evidence: Compare numeric instance addresses with list positions. A shifted index can associate a remaining name with a different existing object.
Move to stable keyed identities with an explicit migration plan, or otherwise preserve intended address mappings. Avoid applying unintended replacements.
Check a full plan for only the intended removal and verify surviving remote identities remain unchanged.

references.title: Count removal replaces wrong instance — primary documentation

debugging.title: Imported object immediately changes
debugging.symptom: After import, Terraform proposes a disruptive update to an existing resource.

steps.evidence: Compare imported attributes, configuration defaults and immutable fields. Import establishes identity but does not make configuration match reality.
Write accurate configuration and intentionally decide which differences to manage. Review provider-specific replacement behavior before any apply.
Obtain an expected plan and test dependent behavior after any approved changes.

references.title: Imported object immediately changes — primary documentation

debugging.title: Wrong environment selected
debugging.symptom: A plan shows resources from a different environment than expected.

steps.evidence: Check workspace, backend key, account credentials, region and variable files. A correct workspace name alone does not prove correct credentials.
Stop before apply and correct the target configuration. Regenerate the plan; do not reuse a file created against the wrong target.
Confirm caller identity, backend and expected resource addresses, then review the newly generated plan.

debugging.title: Provider upgrade creates broad diff
debugging.symptom: Updating provider dependencies produces many unexpected changes.

steps.evidence: Compare lock-file versions, release notes and schema/default changes. Separate actual infrastructure drift from changed provider interpretation.
Pin back to the known-compatible version if needed and test the upgrade independently. Resolve migration requirements before combining it with other changes.
Run representative plans and a controlled canary apply; confirm no unrelated replacements before wider rollout.

references.title: Provider upgrade creates broad diff — primary documentation

debugging.title: Targeted recovery leaves drift
debugging.symptom: A targeted apply fixed one resource, but the system remains inconsistent.

steps.evidence: Run a full plan and inspect resources omitted by targeting, including downstream dependencies and outputs.
Reconcile remaining changes through a reviewed full operation. Keep targeting exceptional rather than making it the normal deployment path.
Confirm a subsequent full plan is clean or contains only explicitly accepted differences and application checks pass.

references.title: Targeted recovery leaves drift — primary documentation
